newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia pledges troops for neutral Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia pledges troops for neutral Zaire force.

text.p: Ethiopia pledged on Wednesday to contribute troops to a neutral force to protect refugees in eastern Zaire if approved by the U.N. Security Council.

"Ethiopia is committed to extend its contribution to the neutral force whose deployment is subject to U.N. Security Council approval," Foreign Minister Seyoum Mesfin told the state Ethiopian News Agency.

"East African countries and those in the Great Lakes Region which met in Nairobi to discuss the crisis in eastern Zaire have also the responsibility to take part in the formation of the neutral force," he added.

Seyoum said African leaders attending the Nairobi summit as well as Ethiopia's Prime Minister Meles Zenawi on Tuesday agreed the foreign ministers of Ethiopia, Kenya and Tanzania and an Organisation of African Unity representative would go to Zaire.
They would pass the decisions of the summit to the government of Zaire and also push for a ceasefire, he added.

The eight-nation Nairobi summit called for a neutral protection force for the 1.2 million refugees in eastern Zaire and requested the Security Council deploy such a force to establish safe aid corridors and temporary sanctuaries.
